issues.label: Problem 1
issues.status: Demonstrated incompatibility in the acquired version's literal general-metric face prescription and claimed special-Lagrangian cylinder.

source_location.claim: Section 2.3's first face prescription; the model used by Proposition 2.30, Lemma 3.8 and Theorem 1.3(2).

issues.hypotheses: n=3; real symmetric positive-definite ambient matrix G=[[A,b],[b^T,c]] with c>0; face x3=0 and x1,x2>0, x1+x2<pi; printed potential u_A=Phi/sqrt(det A); Omega_G is exactly the source's lower-index ambient form; claimed phase pi.
issues.suspect_step: The printed face data use the ambient principal submatrix A, while the cylinder's special phase depends on S=A-b*b^T/c. Treating that prescribed lower-dimensional potential as a same-phase cylindrical solution is unjustified when b is nonzero.

decisive_evidence.general_identity: Omega_G(F_x1,F_x2,F_t)=i*c*det(I+i*S*H); Im(exp(-i*pi)*Omega_G)=c*(det(S)*det(H)-1). With det(H)=1/det(A), the residual is -b^T*A^{-1}*b.
decisive_evidence.example: G=[[1,0,1/2],[0,1,0],[1/2,0,1]], eigenvalues 1/2,1,3/2. At x1=x2=pi/3 on x3=0, H=[[2,1],[1,2]]/sqrt(3), det(H)=1, the Lagrangian pullback is zero and the phase-pi residual is exactly -1/4 for every y3.
decisive_evidence.limit_argument: A translated C1 limit of phase-pi special Lagrangians in these translation-invariant ambient forms must have zero phase residual. The claimed exponential C^{k,alpha} normal-graph asymptote implies such a limit, contradicting the displayed nonzero residual.

method: Complete analytic block-determinant calculation and positivity check
Explicit example satisfying all ambient and relative-face hypotheses
Analytic continuity-of-pullback argument for the claimed C1 limit
Independent exact SymPy confirmation, not floating-point sampling
counterevidence_and_alternatives: The inverse of the induced position-space face metric is S, not A. This offers an intended repair but changes the literal printed coefficient.
The case b=0 has S=A and no obstruction of this type; the two-dimensional formula remains valid.
A linear coordinate change standardizing G also changes simplex coordinates/face coefficients and cannot retain the unchanged printed prescription.
Orientation, phase modulo pi, positive normalization of Omega, and affine shifts of the potential cannot remove a nonzero phase residual.
No numerical construction of a hypothetical u3 is required because the proven contradiction concerns simultaneous validity of the printed prescription and the asserted asymptote.

repair.statement: For this cylinder replace u_A by u_S=Phi/sqrt(det S).
repair.proof: Then det(D2u_S)=1/det S, so the proved residual identity gives zero. The Lagrangian condition is unchanged, and exp(-i*pi)*Omega_G=c*tr(S*D2u_S)>0. The example gives Omega=-7/3 and residual zero.
repair.verified_scope: Local cylindrical phase and Lagrangian compatibility only.
repair.unverified_scope: All-face induction, boundary compatibility, revised barriers/PDEs, global existence, smoothness and topology for the revised construction.

issues.dependency: Explicit face data -> Proposition 2.30 and Lemma 3.8 -> Theorem 1.3(2).
issues.severity_basis: The affected object is the central comparison solution and asymptotic model for general allowed matrices, rather than a peripheral estimate. This is a demonstrated obstruction to the printed proof/construction package, not a universal nonexistence result.

unresolved_scope: Whether a complete all-face induced-metric reformulation proves the intended global statements is not resolved here.
Presence or correction of the issue in the journal-final text is not established.
External PDE/geometric-measure-theory dependencies elsewhere were not independently reproved.
main_theorem_refuted_scope: No independent disproof of the existence, smoothness or topology conclusion of Theorem 1.2; the literal prescription/asymptote package is incompatible.
